answer: An applicant locks a refundable bond and is assigned a one-shot field checkpoint at a mapped canyon site. The device must emit a receipt signed by a sealed quartz timing module that cannot be cloned without destroying the key. Reviewers open the books only at the zenith of the admission window and cluster those receipts: identical clocks, reused paths, or copy-pasted traces slash the bond. Standing up many aliases then requires many bonds and many unique modules, so one honest identity stays cheaper than a farm.
